### Running evals as an account

A run with no saved account choice acts a
s the server's **default** account.\nTo run evals from CI as one account, upload its token, make it the default,\nthen start the r

un:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PATCH \
 "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/
servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: applic

ation/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI takes the same steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, whic

h
reads the token from a file, an environment variable or stdin, and
`mcpjam cloud server-accounts default`. See the
[CLI refer
ence](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts-commands).\n\nThe default is shared by every run that key sta
rts, so don't run the same\nkey's runs at the same time with different defaults. Where your organization\nhas account choice for e
val suites, a suite can instead save the accounts it\nruns as, in its settings in the app; a run with a saved choice uses those\na

ccounts and ignores the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELETE` removes the account and its stored token, and asks the tok
en's issuer\nto revoke the token where the issuer supports revocation. That is best effort,\nand it also ends any copy of the same
token you still hold. The default\naccount can't be deleted while other accounts exist (`409`): make another\naccount the default

first.

### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens` still works, and is removed 90 days after the
accoun
ts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating an unnamed\none when the server has none, and keeps its old body and
its old\n`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a\n`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `.../account

s`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An existing default it writes
into keeps whatever rule it had. Its `serverUr
l` must be the URL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`\nand `tokens.id_tok

en` are accepted and ignored. Move to
`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which names the account it writes.

The error codes these r
outes add to `details.code` are listed in the\n[error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md#serve

r-account-errors).

## Run evals from the API

The shortest useful loop — create a run with one inline test, then poll:

```
bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\n# 1. Create (responds 202 immediately; -f + jq -e fail fast on errors)\nRUN_ID=$(curl -f
sS -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY
\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n \"suiteName\": \"smoke\",\n \"serverIds\": [\"'$SERVER_ID'\"],\

n "tests": [{
 "title": "echo works",
 "runs": 1,
 "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5",
\"provider\": \"anthropic\",\n \"steps\": [\n { \"id\": \"s1\", \"kind\": \"prompt\", \"prompt\": \"Use the echo tool
url -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"

# 3. If it did not pass, read the decision summary FIRST
curl -s "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-ru
ns/$RUN_ID/decision-summary\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"\n\n# 4. Or go straight to per-iteration tool call
s, token usage, latency\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/iterations\" \\\n -H \"Au

thorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"
```

The decision summary composes steps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so every
clie
nt reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating on it:\n\n* **`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** Under per
-case grading the\n counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials inside them;\n under a suite-wide accuracy t
hreshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a different total under each — 3 against 15 for three cases run five times —\n
so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted\n across that line.\n* **It explains the verdict; it n
ever re-decides it.** The run's own decision is\n the authority and is carried through on `decision`. The per-trial\n `diagnosti
cs` sit underneath it — a case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tallying diagnostics gives a different answer than the p
latform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not `inconclusive`.** It\n means no verdict exists at al
l (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decision — the validity\n
phase ran and withheld a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the whole list.** A page\n fetched with a `cu

rsor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates
 "nothing failed" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scoped t
o the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span\nids, prompt indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's row a

lone,
and `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you can append to your base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` takes
an id from the hosted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.\n`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` — and runs on your organization's credits
.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't e
xecute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the valid\nhosted ids for that provider.\
n\nReruns are even shorter: `{ \"suiteId\": \"...\" }` reruns the suite exactly as\nconfigured, connecting the suite's saved serve
r selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no saved

selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with
`details.reason: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running agains

t a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite that has
it **attached**. Attac
h them first with\n`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach them
all; `[]` is rejected — use `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attached\nenvironments;
anything else is a `400` with\n`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED\"`, raised before any case is\nauthored or any server

connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:

* **no** attached environments → the run uses t
he saved server selection, as before;\n* **exactly one** attached → that environment is used automatically. The `202`\n response'
s `environment` field says so;\n* **several** attached → `400` with `details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED\"`,\n naming the cand

idates.

The environment supplies the closed server set — including the servers its
pinned plugin versions contribute — so `ser
verIds` is not required and is\n**rejected** alongside it (`400`), rather than accepted and ignored: honoring\nboth would connect
a different set than the run is stamped with. The same goes\nfor a `serverIds` override on an environment-based suite\n(`details.r

eason: "ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE"`).

The run is pinned to the environment revision resolved at launch: if the
env
ironment changes in between, the run is rejected with `CONFLICT` (409)\nrather than executing against a different configuration th

an the one whose
tools were captured. Use
`GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` to see what it
will
connect before launching.\n\nWhen creating a new inline suite, `POST .../eval-runs` also accepts `hosts: [{ host: \"Claude\", serv
